rationale: flops-3 is a tiny, compute-bound floating-point benchmark dominated by hot arithmetic loops with no meaningful static profile available, so the table favors low-overhead passes and suppresses loop-inflating ones: BCF gets a high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weight (0.9/0.8) so its opaque predicates are applied sparingly since they would devastate FLOPS-loop iteration cost, and FLA is similarly damped (0.7 runtime) because flattening dispatch loops in hot code is expensive, while both retain high SecurityGain/DiversityGain (0.8/0.7) so they still fire on cold functions whose features favor those dimensions; SUB is kept moderately active (low runtime cost) but with a nonzero CorrectnessRisk weight (0.3) reflecting that substitution on floating-point expressions can perturb numerics and should apply conservatively; SPLIT and IGV are cheap structural/global-variable transforms with negligible runtime/size impact and are left broadly enabled to add diversity at essentially no cost; IBR and ICALL sit in the middle, providing control-flow and call-graph indirection that resist static analysis without the multiplicative loop overhead of BCF/FLA, with ICALL's CorrectnessRisk slightly raised because indirect-call rewriting can interact badly with float-heavy straight-line code; overall this biases selection toward diverse low-cost transforms spread across all functions rather than heavy passes concentrated in hot loops, preserving the benchmark's runtime envelope and exact FP semantics.
